does_not_close: No FTO, no legal advice, no clearance opinion. This is a re-derivation exercise over the fixture's own claim-charted families using public patent text already on disk.

The 'broad / practitioner-cautious' construction for family n=1 is presented as a REASONABLE alternative a competent, cautious FTO counsel could adopt -- not as a definitive infringement conclusion. Whether counsel would ultimately adopt it requires prosecution-history review (file wrapper, any examiner remarks on 'about 70 percent' during examination) which this audit does not perform.
Does not modify the manifest (66 receipts / 11 modules), the pinned patent_landscape.json fixture, or any signed Phase-0 KPI.
AUDIT_ONLY: promotes no authority and flips no scientific_readiness.

headline: Family n=1 (WO2016187380A1): the fixture's bright-line 'reads_on_ours: NO' rests in part on treating claim 1's hedge-qualified 'volume solids content of greater than about 70 percent' as a bare, unqualified 70% threshold. Re-reading the ACTUAL claim text and the specification's own disclosed 'high volume solids' embodiment ranges (which extend down to 'about 50%' and '60% to about 95%' for the identical concept) shows a reasonable, spec-informed construction under which a ~65% VS coating is not confidently excluded. This is a genuine claim-construction-sensitivity flip: 4/5 tested families (n=2,3,4,5) are robust across all three constructions tested (narrow, plain, broad); n=1 is not.
non_circularity: Real claim-1 text is independently re-derived from the same hash-pinned raw HTML snapshots the prior claim-chart-provenance-v1 audit already fetched and pinned (SHA256 re-verified below, byte-for-byte, before use); this run performs no new network fetch. Constructions are applied to the REAL claim text and the REAL specification disclosure, not to the fixture's paraphrase.
purpose: Falsification attack on the claim: 'The FTO screen's conclusions are robust to reasonable variation in how patent claims are construed', restricted to the 6 claim-charted families in patent_landscape.json (independent_claim_chart.charted=true).

constructions.basis: Fixture `why` field treats the limitation as a bare threshold: 'our VS ~65% (<70%)'.
constructions.construed_scope: volume solids content > 70.0% exactly, no tolerance
constructions.name: narrow (fixture-implicit)

constructions.basis: Real claim 1 text (independently re-derived, quoted below) says 'volume solids content of greater than about 70 percent', not a bare '70 percent'. A POSA applying ordinary claim-construction practice to an 'about'-qualified numeric limitation gives it a modest tolerance tied to the field's own measurement reproducibility (ASTM D2697 / D5201 volume-solids determinations are typically reproducible to a few points, not to +/-5 points).
constructions.construed_scope: volume solids content roughly >= 67-68% (small 'about' tolerance around 70%)
constructions.name: plain/ordinary (POSA, hedge honored, modest tolerance)

constructions.basis: The specification's own general description of the invention (quoted below) discloses OVERLAPPING 'high volume solids' embodiment ranges for the same concept the claim numerically pins at 'about 70 percent': 'about 50% to about 100%', '60% to about 95%', and '70% to about 90%'. FTO counsel construing an ambiguous, hedge-qualified numeric term is expected to adopt the reading LEAST favorable to a clean-exclusion conclusion (i.e. the broadest reading a competent adversary could press), not the reading most convenient for the screen. Read in light of the spec's own lower embodiment floors for the identical 'high volume solids' concept, 'about 70 percent' is not demonstrably a hard, isolated 70.0% cutoff -- a coating at ~65% VS sits inside two of the three disclosed embodiment ranges for the same invention concept ('about 50% to about 100%' and '60% to about 95%'), so it cannot be confidently excluded on this limitation alone without further quantitative work the fixture does not do.
constructions.construed_scope: volume solids content within the invention's own disclosed 'high volume solids' embodiment space (as low as ~50-60%), not a rigid 70.0% line
constructions.name: broad / specification-informed, practitioner-cautious

results.note_on_other_limitation: Family 1's NO also rests on a second, independent limitation ('no distinct reactive polar compatibilizer', claim-1 component (c)). That element was separately checked: claim 1 requires component (c) as a THIRD, distinct ingredient beyond (a) epoxy and (b) polyamide hardener; our_primer_assumed lists epoxy + polyamide hardener + silica extender + iron-oxide color + solvent -- no third reactive/polar component under any construction tested (narrow, plain, or broad functional reading of 'reactive compatibilizer agent ... having at least one polar functionality'). This element does NOT flip; only the volume-solids element does.

constructions.basis: Fixture: 'a specific micronized polyamide RHEOLOGY additive, not a curing agent'.

constructions.name: narrow (fixture-implicit)

constructions.basis: Real claim 1 (quoted below) requires 'a median particle size ranging from 1 um to 10 um'. A liquid curative has no median particle size in the ordinary sense a POSA in coatings/rheology additives would apply the term (a solid-particulate distribution measurement); the term does not read on a bulk liquid under its plain meaning.
constructions.name: plain/ordinary (POSA)

constructions.basis: Even reading 'particle size' as broadly as the specification allows (dispersed/emulsified droplet form is discussed elsewhere in the spec for handling), our_primer_assumed's 'dimer-acid reactive polyamide' is compositionally a condensation product of DIMER fatty acids with polyamines -- chemically outside the claim's own closed acid set (diamine limited to ethylene/hexamethylene diamine; monoacid limited to acetic/propionic; fatty acid limited to 12-hydroxystearic/lesquerolic). 'Consisting essentially of' this specific triad forecloses a broad reading that would sweep in a structurally different dimer-acid curative.
constructions.construed_scope: closed triad (specified diamine + specified monoacid + specified fatty acid), any form
constructions.name: broad / practitioner-cautious

constructions.basis: Fixture: 'primary has no zinc phosphate; Enhanced-65 has zinc phosphate alone, with no molybdate/benzoate'.
constructions.construed_scope: consisting essentially of ALL THREE: zinc phosphate + zinc molybdate + zinc benzoate salt, each within its stated parts-by-weight window
constructions.name: narrow (fixture-implicit)

constructions.basis: 'Consisting essentially of' (a recognized intermediate transitional phrase) still requires the basic and novel characteristic -- here, presence of all three named zinc salts -- to be met; it does not excuse ABSENCE of a required component, only tolerate unlisted non-material additions.
constructions.name: plain/ordinary (POSA)

constructions.basis: No construction of 'consisting essentially of X, Y, and Z' can be stretched to cover a formulation missing X entirely (primary) or missing Y and Z entirely (Enhanced-65); this is a presence/absence question, not an interpretive-boundary question, so breadth of construction cannot supply an absent ingredient. (Separately, the patent is EXPIRED ~2003 by fee lapse, so a flip here would not even change FTO risk -- noted for completeness, not relied upon for the construction verdict.)
constructions.name: broad / practitioner-cautious

theory_reference: Phillips v. AWH Corp., 415 F.3d 1303 (Fed. Cir. 2005) (en banc) -- claims construed in light of the specification and prosecution history, not in isolation; Pall Corp. v. Micron Separations, Inc., 66 F.3d 1211 (Fed. Cir. 1995) -- 'about'/approximation terms construed by context, breadth varies with specification support; MPEP 2111.01 -- broadest reasonable interpretation informs how a competent, cautious practitioner should treat an ambiguous claim term for clearance purposes.
